scenario: 面试官说「你的模型 precision 已经 92% 了，还能做什么？」——想看你会不会往下深挖失败。
scenario_en: The interviewer says 'your model is already at 92% precision, what else would you do?' — probing whether you dig into failures.
q: error analysis 到底是什么？它和 debugging 有什么不同？
q_en: What is error analysis, and how is it different from debugging?
why: error analysis 是系统性收集/归类/诊断失败样例、找可落地根因（数据/架构/特征）的设计技能，产出会改数据采集、架构、监控、上线；debugging 只是修单个报错。主动讲这套流程是 L5 而非 L4 的成熟度信号。
why_en: Error analysis is a design skill that systematically collects, categorizes, and diagnoses failures to find actionable root causes, unlike debugging which just fixes one crash.
diagram:
flowchart LR C["1. Collect
分层抽样失败"] --> K["2. Categorize
互斥穷尽打标"] K --> M["3. Map to root cause
追到组件→设计动作"]
options: error analysis 就是 debugging——逐条修线上报错、让服务别崩，和模型怎么设计无关
只看 aggregate 指标（precision/recall/AUC）定好坏，指标达标就收工，不必逐类拆失败
系统性收集/归类/诊断失败样例找可落地根因，据此改数据、架构、监控、上线，是设计技能
直接堆模型容量（加层、加参数）把错误压下去，用规模换准确率
options_en: Error analysis is just debugging — fix each production crash so the service stays up, unrelated to model design.
Only read aggregate metrics (precision/recall/AUC) to judge quality; once they pass, stop — no need to break down failures.
Systematically collect, categorize, and diagnose failures to find actionable root causes, then change data, architecture, monitoring, and rollout — a design skill.
Just pile on model capacity (more layers, more params) to crush the errors, trading scale for accuracy.
optionExplanations: 把它当 debugging 就漏掉了核心：error analysis 的产出是设计决策（改数据/架构/监控），不是修一个 bug 让服务复活。
aggregate 指标正是它要突破的——92% 的均值能盖住某个高危小类的系统性错分，只看均值就发现不了。
对；这一整套「收集→归类→根因」正是把失败翻译成设计动作，区别于就事论事的 debugging。
没做归类就加容量，等于不知道是数据问题还是模型问题就乱开药；很多失败是数据缺口，堆容量白费。
optionExplanations_en: Treating it as debugging misses the point: error analysis outputs design decisions (change data/architecture/monitoring), not a one-off bug fix.
Aggregate metrics are exactly what it breaks past — a 92% average can hide systematic misclassification of one high-risk minority slice.
Correct — the full collect-categorize-root-cause loop translates failures into design actions, unlike case-by-case debugging.
Adding capacity before categorizing is prescribing blind; many failures are data gaps where more capacity is wasted.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统性收集、归类、诊断失败样例，找到可落地根因并转成设计动作的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Error analysis is the process of systematically collecting, categorizing, and diagnosing failure cases to find actionable root causes and turn them into design actions.

termDefinitions.meaning: ROC 曲线下面积，衡量分类器区分正负样本的总体能力，0.5 为随机、1 为完美。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) measures a classifier's overall ability to rank positives above negatives, 0.5 being random and 1 perfect.

scenario: 一个内容分类器整体 precision 92%，但某个「高危违规类别」样本量很小，占比不到 2%。
scenario_en: A content classifier reports 92% overall precision, but one high-risk violation category is tiny, under 2% of samples.
q: 为什么不能只看 aggregate precision 就上线？
q_en: Why can't you ship on aggregate precision alone?
why: 均值是按样本量加权的，多数类一好就把少数高危类的系统性错分「数学上淹没」掉——92% 的表面数字里可能藏着某个 2% 小类几乎全错。所以要按 slice 拆开看，均值必要但不充分。
why_en: The aggregate is sample-weighted, so a strong majority mathematically drowns out systematic failures in a small high-risk slice, making the average necessary but insufficient.
options: 均值已经代表所有子群，92% 说明每个类别都至少 92%，可以直接上线
均值按样本量加权，多数类会淹没 2% 高危类的系统性错分，必须按 slice 拆开验收
precision 高就不用看 recall，漏检问题在高 precision 下不会发生
小类样本少所以不重要，2% 的类别就算全错也不影响业务
options_en: The average already represents every subgroup, so 92% means each category is at least 92% — ship it.
The average is sample-weighted, so the majority drowns out systematic errors in the 2% high-risk class; you must break it down per slice.
High precision means you can ignore recall — missed detections don't happen when precision is high.
Small classes don't matter, so even if the 2% category is all wrong it won't affect the business.
optionExplanations: 均值不等于逐类下限：整体 92% 完全可能是 98% 的大类 + 40% 的小类加权出来的，逐类下限可能远低于 92%。
对；加权均值天然偏向多数类，高危小类的错分被稀释看不见，只有 per-slice 指标才暴露它。
precision 和 recall 是两回事：高 precision 说明报出来的多为真，但对漏检（FN）一无所知。
高危类恰恰是「样本少但单次代价高」的典型，2% 全错在内容审核里可能就是灾难性放行。
optionExplanations_en: The average is not a per-class floor: 92% overall can be 98% majority plus 40% minority weighted together, so a class can be far below 92%.
Correct — a weighted average favors the majority and dilutes the high-risk minority's errors; only per-slice metrics expose them.
Precision and recall are different: high precision says flagged items are mostly right but says nothing about missed detections (FN).
High-risk classes are exactly the 'few samples, high per-case cost' case; 2% all-wrong in moderation can mean catastrophic passes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按某个维度（类别/地区/设备）划出的评估子集，用来单独看模型在该子群上的表现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A slice is an evaluation subset defined by some dimension (category/region/device) to inspect model performance on that subgroup alone.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预测为正的样本里真正为正的比例，TP/(TP+FP)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision is the fraction of predicted-positive samples that are truly positive, TP/(TP+FP).

q: 把 Google/Meta 的错误分析三阶段工作流排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the Google/Meta three-phase error-analysis workflow:
steps: 把每一类失败追到具体组件（数据管线/特征库/架构/后处理），转成设计动作
从线上日志或评估集分层抽样失败样例
人工给每个失败打互斥且穷尽（MECE）的类别标签：缺特征/标签噪声/分布漂移…
why: 顺序是 Collect（分层抽样失败）→ Categorize（MECE 打标）→ Map（追到组件转设计动作）。跳过 Categorize 直接从失败跳到改模型，是最常见错误——你根本分不清是数据问题还是模型问题。
why_en: The order is Collect via stratified sampling, then Categorize with MECE labels, then Map each category to a component and a design action.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["Collect
分层抽样"] --> B["Categorize
MECE 打标"] B --> C["Map
组件→设计动作"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 互斥且穷尽：每个失败恰好落进一个类别，且所有类别覆盖全部失败。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MECE (Mutually Exclusive, Collectively Exhaustive) means every failure falls into exactly one category and the categories cover all failures.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按子群比例分层取样，避免均匀抽样过度代表多数类、埋掉少数类失败。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Stratified sampling draws samples per subgroup so majority classes don't crowd out minority failures the way uniform sampling does.

scenario: 要从线上日志里抽一批失败样例做人工分析，多数流量来自主流市场、主流内容类型，边缘 case 占比很小。
scenario_en: You need to sample failures from prod logs for manual analysis; most traffic is mainstream markets/content, with edge cases a tiny share.
q: Collect 阶段该用均匀抽样还是分层抽样？
q_en: For the Collect phase, uniform sampling or stratified sampling?
why: 分层抽样：按 segment/内容类型/边缘 case 分层取，保证少数群体的失败进得来。均匀抽样会过度代表多数类，把少数类的失败埋掉，等于一开始就看不见问题。
why_en: Use stratified sampling across segments and edge cases so minority failures are represented, because uniform sampling over-represents the majority and buries the minority.
tradeoff: 分层抽样（覆盖少数类、能发现小样本失败）vs 均匀抽样（简单但过度代表多数类）
whenOtherWins: 如果你只想估计整体失败率、且各子群失败模式已知相似，均匀抽样的无偏估计更省事也够用。
options: 均匀随机抽样，反映真实流量分布，主流内容多抽点最能代表现状
分层抽样，按 segment/内容类型/边缘 case 分层取，保证少数群体的失败也进样本
只抽置信度最高的错分，因为模型最确信却错的样例信息量最大
只抽多数类，样本量大统计更稳，少数类等以后有空再单独看
options_en: Uniform random sampling to reflect real traffic — mainstream content dominating best represents the status quo.
Stratified sampling across segments/content-types/edge-cases so minority-group failures also make it into the sample.
Only sample the highest-confidence misclassifications, since the model's most-confident-yet-wrong cases carry the most signal.
Only sample the majority class — larger samples are statistically stabler; look at minority classes later when there's time.
optionExplanations: 均匀抽样复刻的是流量分布，而流量本身就偏向多数类；结果是少数高危类的失败几乎抽不到。
对；分层保证每个子群都有代表，才可能在 Categorize 阶段发现「某小类失败集中」这种可行动模式。
只看高置信错分（hard negative）是 ranking 里的一招，但作为 Collect 的唯一策略会漏掉低置信的系统性失败。
只抽多数类正是要避免的偏差——你会得到一个「大类很好」的假象，而问题都藏在没抽到的小类里。
optionExplanations_en: Uniform sampling mirrors traffic, which itself skews to the majority, so minority high-risk failures barely get sampled.
Correct — stratification represents every subgroup, enabling Categorize to reveal actionable 'one small class fails a lot' patterns.
Sampling only high-confidence errors (hard negatives) is one ranking trick, but as the sole Collect strategy it misses low-confidence systematic failures.
Sampling only the majority is the exact bias to avoid — you get a false 'majority is great' picture while the problems hide in the unsampled minority.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按用户或内容属性划出的群体，如新用户、某地区、某内容类别。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A segment is a group defined by user or content attributes, e.g. new users, a region, or a content category.

scenario: Categorize 阶段要给每个失败人工打标签，可选类别有「缺特征、标签噪声、分布漂移、模型容量、serving 延迟截断」。
scenario_en: In Categorize, you manually label each failure with categories like missing-feature, label-noise, distribution-shift, model-capacity, serving-latency-truncation.
q: 这套失败类别体系必须满足什么性质？
q_en: What property must this failure-category taxonomy satisfy?
why: 类别必须互斥且穷尽（MECE）：每个失败恰好进一个桶，所有桶覆盖全部失败。这样才能算出可信的占比（如 45% 缺特征），进而把最大那类根因锁定成设计动作。
why_en: Categories must be mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive so each failure lands in exactly one bucket and proportions are trustworthy.
whenOtherWins: 早期探索、还不知道有哪些失败模式时，可以先用开放标签自由记录，等模式浮现再收敛成 MECE 桶。
options: 类别越多越好，一个失败可以同时打多个标签，覆盖面才全
类别互斥且穷尽（MECE）：每个失败恰好进一个桶，所有桶覆盖全部失败
只需要一个「模型不够好」的大类，先把失败都归进去再说
标签必须和最终修复方案一一对应，否则不算有效类别
options_en: The more categories the better, and one failure can carry several labels at once for full coverage.
Categories are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive (MECE): each failure lands in exactly one bucket and the buckets cover all failures.
You only need one big 'model not good enough' bucket — dump all failures there first.
Labels must map one-to-one to the final fix, or they don't count as valid categories.
optionExplanations: 允许一个失败打多标签，占比就没法相加、也没法说清「哪类最大」，Categorize 的诊断价值就没了。
对；MECE 是能算占比、定优先级的前提，也是区分「数据问题 vs 模型问题」的第一步。
一个「模型不够好」的桶正是要避免的——它把数据缺口、标签噪声全糊在一起，导向错误的加容量修复。
类别是诊断维度，不必和修复一一对应；同一类根因可能对应多种修复，反之亦然。
optionExplanations_en: Allowing multi-label failures makes proportions non-additive and blurs 'which is largest', destroying Categorize's diagnostic value.
Correct — MECE is the prerequisite for computing proportions and priorities, and the first step to separate data vs model problems.
One 'model not good enough' bucket is exactly what to avoid — it blends data gaps and label noise, pushing a wrong add-capacity fix.
Categories are diagnostic dimensions, not one-to-one with fixes; one root cause can map to several fixes and vice versa.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线上数据分布偏离训练分布，导致模型在新分布上表现下降。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Distribution shift is when live data drifts away from the training distribution, degrading the model on the new distribution.

termDefinitions.term: serving latency truncation / 服务延迟截断
termDefinitions.meaning: 为满足延迟预算在推理时截断特征或计算，牺牲了预测质量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Serving latency truncation is cutting features or computation at inference to meet a latency budget, sacrificing prediction quality.

scenario: 同事看到一批失败样例，直接说「模型不行，我们加大模型、多训几轮」。
scenario_en: A teammate sees a batch of failures and jumps straight to 'the model is weak, let's scale it up and train more'.
q: 从失败直接跳到改模型，最大的风险是什么？
q_en: What's the biggest risk of jumping from failures straight to model changes?
why: 跳过 Categorize 就分不清数据问题和模型问题，很可能开错药方：明明是数据缺口（新实体没历史），你却去加容量，钱花了错误照旧。这是错误分析里最常见的错误。
why_en: Skipping Categorize means you can't tell a data problem from a model problem, so you likely apply the wrong fix — adding capacity to what is really a data gap.
options: 没有风险，加大模型总能提升指标，是最稳妥的第一步
分不清是数据问题还是模型问题，容易开错药方——数据缺口却去加容量，白花钱
唯一风险是训练变慢，指标本身一定会随容量单调上升
风险只在于 A/B 测试要多跑几天，方向本身没错
options_en: No risk — scaling the model always lifts metrics, so it's the safest first move.
You can't tell a data problem from a model problem, so you likely misprescribe — adding capacity to what is really a data gap, wasting money.
The only risk is slower training; the metric itself will rise monotonically with capacity.
The only risk is the A/B test running a few extra days; the direction itself is fine.
optionExplanations: 加容量并非万能：如果失败源于新实体没历史特征，再大的模型也变不出不存在的信号。
对；Categorize 正是用来分「数据 vs 模型」，跳过它做决策就是蒙——最常见的翻车点。
指标不会随容量单调上升，数据缺口类失败对容量几乎不敏感，learning curve 会平掉。
方向可能根本错了：把数据问题当模型问题修，A/B 再久也测不出该有的提升。
optionExplanations_en: More capacity isn't a cure-all: if failures stem from new entities lacking history features, no bigger model conjures nonexistent signal.
Correct — Categorize is what separates data vs model; deciding without it is guessing, the most common blowup.
Metrics don't rise monotonically with capacity; data-gap failures are nearly insensitive to capacity and the learning curve flattens.
The direction may be wrong: fixing a data problem as a model problem means no A/B will show the expected lift.

termDefinitions.meaning: 误差随训练数据量变化的曲线，用来判断「加数据还有没有用」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A learning curve plots error versus training-data volume, used to judge whether more data still helps.

scenario: 欺诈检测里，漏报（FN）集中出现在「新商户」（交易 <10 笔）身上。
scenario_en: In fraud detection, false negatives cluster on new merchants with fewer than 10 transactions.
q: 把这个欺诈漏报案例的错误分析推理链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the reasoning chain for this fraud-FN error-analysis case:
steps: 根因 = 数据缺口（新商户没交易历史），不是模型不够强
观察到欺诈 FN 聚集在新商户（<10 笔交易）
修复 = 从 onboarding 信号造辅助特征（业务类型/验证状态/注册时长），而非换更大模型
归类为『缺特征』而不是『模型容量』
why: 链条：观察 FN 聚集 → 归类『缺特征』→ 根因是数据缺口 → 修复用 onboarding 辅助特征。关键在于归类那一步把方向从「加容量」扳到「补数据」，最后落到具体特征而不是更大模型。
why_en: Observe FN clustering, categorize as missing-feature, trace to a data gap, then fix with onboarding-derived auxiliary features rather than a bigger model.

termDefinitions.meaning: 假阴性：实际为正（欺诈）却被判为负（放行），在欺诈检测里代价很高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FN (False Negative) is a truly-positive case (fraud) predicted negative (approved), costly in fraud detection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 商户注册时可得的信息（业务类型、验证状态、注册时长），可在无交易历史时当辅助特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Onboarding signals are info available at signup (business type, verification, registration recency) usable as auxiliary features when transaction history is absent.

scenario: 错误分析发现 70% 的欺诈漏报（FN）落在新商户（交易 <10 笔）上，其余商户表现正常。
scenario_en: Error analysis shows 70% of fraud false negatives fall on new merchants (<10 transactions), while other merchants are fine.
q: 最该采取的修复是什么？
q_en: What's the right fix?
why: 这是数据/特征缺口（新商户没历史），不是容量、阈值或数据量问题。修复应从 onboarding 数据造辅助特征，再加一条针对新账户的定向策略规则；换大模型或降阈值都治不了「信号根本不存在」。
why_en: It's a data/feature gap on new merchants, so engineer features from onboarding data plus a targeted new-account policy rule, not a bigger model or lower threshold.
tradeoff: 补 onboarding 特征 + 新账户策略规则（治数据缺口）vs 加容量/降阈值（治不了缺信号）
whenOtherWins: 如果 FN 均匀分布在各类商户、且 learning curve 显示加数据还在降错误，那才是容量或数据量问题，扩模型/加样本才对症。
options: 换一个更大容量的模型并多训几轮，用规模压低这批漏报
全局调低分类阈值，让更多交易被判为欺诈以减少漏报
从 onboarding 数据给新商户造辅助特征，并加一条针对新账户的定向策略规则
再多标 10 倍训练样本，靠数据量把新商户这类学好
options_en: Swap in a higher-capacity model and train more epochs to crush these misses with scale.
Lower the global classification threshold so more transactions are flagged as fraud, reducing misses.
Engineer auxiliary features for new merchants from onboarding data, plus a targeted policy rule for new accounts.
Label 10x more training samples and let sheer data volume teach the new-merchant case.
optionExplanations: 根因是新商户没历史信号，再大的模型也变不出不存在的特征，容量对这类失败几乎无效。
全局降阈值会把大量正常交易误判为欺诈（FP 暴涨），代价转嫁给多数正常商户，治标不治本。
对；缺特征就补特征——onboarding 信号 + 新账户规则直接填上「没历史」这个洞，定向且低副作用。
多标样本对「特征里根本没有的信号」无能为力，learning curve 会平掉，钱花在错误维度。
optionExplanations_en: The root cause is new merchants lacking history signals; no bigger model conjures nonexistent features, so capacity barely helps.
Lowering the global threshold floods normal transactions into fraud (FP spikes), shifting cost to the honest majority — a band-aid.
Correct — a feature gap needs features: onboarding signals plus a new-account rule directly fill the 'no history' hole, targeted and low-side-effect.
More labels can't fix a signal that isn't in the features; the learning curve flattens and money goes to the wrong dimension.

termDefinitions.meaning: 假阳性：实际为负（正常交易）却被判为正（欺诈），在支付里造成误拦友好交易。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FP (False Positive) is a truly-negative case (legit transaction) predicted positive (fraud), causing friction on good payments.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把模型分数转成正/负判断的分界点，调它是在 precision 和 recall 之间挪操作点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The threshold turns a model score into a positive/negative decision; moving it trades precision against recall.

scenario: 分类模型评审时，有人只把混淆矩阵当成「算 precision/recall 的中间表」。
scenario_en: In a classification review, someone treats the confusion matrix as just a scratch table for computing precision/recall.
q: 错误分析里，混淆矩阵应该被当成什么？
q_en: In error analysis, how should you treat the confusion matrix?
why: 把它当诊断仪器，不是指标汇总表：看清 FP 和 FN 各自的代价与结构，再决定操作点。内容审核里 FN（有害内容被放出）远比 FP（误删良性）贵，这会把操作点推向高 recall。
why_en: Treat the confusion matrix as a diagnostic instrument, not a metric summary, so you can weigh the distinct costs of FP versus FN and set the operating point.
options: 一个诊断仪器：分别看清 FP/FN 的代价与结构，据此决定操作点
只是算 precision/recall 的中间表，看完最终两个数就够了
一个用来展示准确率的汇报图，越对角线越满越好，不用管非对角
一个只在训练期有用的调试工具，上线后就不再需要看
options_en: A diagnostic instrument: inspect the distinct costs and structure of FP vs FN, and set the operating point accordingly.
Just a scratch table for precision/recall — once you have the two final numbers, you're done.
A reporting chart for accuracy — the fuller the diagonal the better, and you can ignore the off-diagonal.
A debugging tool useful only during training that you no longer need after launch.
optionExplanations: 对；FP 和 FN 代价常不对称，分开看结构才能把阈值当业务决策来定，而不是当统计副产品。
只取最终两个数就丢了非对角线的结构信息——哪类错、错向哪里，正是诊断的关键。
只盯对角线会忽略 FN 这种高代价错误；内容审核里放行有害内容比误删更该被重点看。
上线后混淆矩阵仍是监控错误结构、发现漂移的持续工具，不是一次性的训练玩具。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — FP and FN costs are often asymmetric, so inspecting structure lets you set the threshold as a business decision, not a statistical byproduct.
Taking only the two final numbers discards off-diagonal structure — which class errs and toward what is the core of diagnosis.
Staring only at the diagonal ignores high-cost FN; in moderation, letting harmful content through deserves more focus than over-removal.
After launch the confusion matrix is still a live tool for monitoring error structure and catching drift, not a one-off training toy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把预测与真实标签交叉列成 TP/FP/FN/TN 四格的表，用来看错分结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A confusion matrix cross-tabulates predictions against true labels into TP/FP/FN/TN cells to reveal error structure.

scenario: 内容审核（Safe / Harmful 两类），要读懂混淆矩阵四格各代表什么代价。
scenario_en: Content moderation (Safe / Harmful); read the four confusion-matrix cells and their costs.
q: 填出内容审核混淆矩阵四格的名称：
q_en: Fill in the four confusion-matrix cells for content moderation:
text: 实际 Safe × 预测 Safe = {{TN}}（无代价）；实际 Safe × 预测 Harmful = {{FP}}（误删良性内容，轻微摩擦）；实际 Harmful × 预测 Safe = {{FN}}（有害内容被放出，代价高）；实际 Harmful × 预测 Harmful = {{TP}}（成功拦截）。
text_en: Actual Safe × Predicted Safe = {{TN}} (no cost); Actual Safe × Predicted Harmful = {{FP}} (benign removed, minor friction); Actual Harmful × Predicted Safe = {{FN}} (harmful shown, high cost); Actual Harmful × Predicted Harmful = {{TP}} (blocked).
why: 记法：以「预测」为准命名 True/False（对不对），以「预测的类」命名 Positive/Negative。这里 FN = 该拦没拦（有害内容放出）是最贵的错，所以操作点要偏 recall。
why_en: True/False says whether the prediction was right and Positive/Negative names the predicted class; here FN (harmful shown) is the costliest error, pushing the operating point toward recall.

termDefinitions.meaning: 真阴性：实际为负、也被判为负（正常内容被放行）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TN (True Negative) is a truly-negative case correctly predicted negative (safe content allowed).

termDefinitions.meaning: 真阳性：实际为正、也被判为正（有害内容被拦）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TP (True Positive) is a truly-positive case correctly predicted positive (harmful content blocked).

scenario: 内容审核里，漏放有害内容（FN）的代价远高于误删良性内容（FP，仅轻微摩擦）。
scenario_en: In moderation, missing harmful content (FN) costs far more than removing benign content (FP, just minor friction).
q: 这种代价不对称应该怎么影响操作点选择？
q_en: How should this cost asymmetry shape the operating point?
why: FN 贵就把操作点往高 recall 推，宁可多误删（FP）也要少漏放（FN），即使 precision 因此下降。阈值是业务决策不是统计最优点——由 product/policy 定，不是 ML 工程师一人拍。
why_en: When FN is costly, push the operating point toward high recall, accepting lower precision, and treat the threshold as a business decision set with product/policy.
tradeoff: 偏高 recall（少漏有害内容，代价是 precision 降、误删增）vs 偏高 precision（少误删，代价是漏放增）
whenOtherWins: 如果场景反过来、FP 才是高代价的（如把合法用户误判欺诈直接封号），就该偏 precision、抬高阈值。
options: 维持默认 0.5 阈值，让统计上的最优点自动平衡两类错误
把操作点推向高 recall，宁可多误删也少漏放，即使 precision 下降；阈值当业务决策定
把操作点推向高 precision，优先保证报出来的都对，漏放多点没关系
同时最大化 precision 和 recall，取两者乘积最大的阈值即可
options_en: Keep the default 0.5 threshold and let the statistical optimum balance the two error types automatically.
Push the operating point toward high recall — accept more over-removal to miss less harm, even as precision drops; set the threshold as a business decision.
Push toward high precision — make sure flagged items are all right, and missing some harm is fine.
Maximize precision and recall at once by picking the threshold that maximizes their product.
optionExplanations: 0.5 只是概率中点，不含代价信息；代价不对称时它绝不是最优操作点。
对；FN 贵就用 recall 换 precision，把阈值下移；这是产品/政策共同拍板的操作点，不是纯统计。
偏 precision 会放大 FN——恰恰是最贵的那类错，方向反了。
『乘积最大』是无代价假设下的机械凑法，忽略了 FN≫FP 这个题目给定的关键约束。
optionExplanations_en: 0.5 is just the probability midpoint carrying no cost info; under asymmetric cost it's never the right operating point.
Correct — when FN is costly, trade precision for recall by lowering the threshold; product/policy own this operating point, not pure stats.
Favoring precision inflates FN — exactly the costliest error, so the direction is backwards.
'Maximize the product' is a mechanical trick under equal costs, ignoring the given FN≫FP constraint.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实际为正的样本里被找出来的比例，TP/(TP+FN)，衡量「漏没漏」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall is the fraction of truly-positive samples the model catches, TP/(TP+FN), measuring how much is missed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 选定阈值后模型落在 precision-recall 曲线上的那个点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The operating point is where the model sits on the precision-recall curve once a threshold is chosen.

scenario: 分类模型有一大批 FN，团队想知道该从哪下手；有人建议先按错误类别把 FN 拆开统计。
scenario_en: A classifier has many FNs; before acting the team stratifies the FNs by error category.
q: 把 FN 按错误类别分层，最可能带来什么价值？
q_en: What's the main value of stratifying FNs by error category?
why: 拆开后常发现某一类占大头（如 60% FN 来自同一个可解决的原因），从而把有限精力集中到影响最大、又能一次修好的那类上。这也是把「模糊的一堆错」变成「可排序的行动项」的关键。
why_en: Stratifying often reveals one addressable cause dominating (e.g. 60% of FNs), letting you focus effort on the highest-impact, fixable category.
tradeoff: 先分层定位大头（集中修最大类）vs 不分层泛泛优化（分散、见效慢）
whenOtherWins: 如果 FN 在各类别上均匀分布、没有明显大头，分层就不会给出优先级，此时该转向 learning-curve 或特征覆盖分析。
options: 能直接把整体 recall 提高，因为分层本身就是一种模型改进
常发现某一类占大头（如 60% FN 同一可解决原因），把精力集中到影响最大且能一次修好的类
能证明模型已经没救，只能重训，用来说服团队推倒重来
主要是为了让报告更好看，把一个数字拆成多个数字显得工作量大
options_en: It directly raises overall recall, because stratification is itself a model improvement.
It often reveals one dominant cause (e.g. 60% of FNs from one addressable reason), focusing effort on the highest-impact, fixable category.
It proves the model is hopeless and must be retrained, useful to convince the team to start over.
It mainly makes the report look bigger by splitting one number into several.
optionExplanations: 分层是分析动作，不改模型也不会自己提升 recall；它只是告诉你该去修哪。
对；找到「60% 来自一个可解决原因」就把模糊的一堆错变成可排序的行动项，性价比最高。
分层往往正好相反——它常显示大头是可定向修复的，不必推倒重来。
拆数字不是为了好看，是为了定位与排优先级；没有大头时才该换分析工具。
optionExplanations_en: Stratifying is an analysis step; without a model change it won't raise recall by itself — it tells you where to fix.
Correct — finding '60% from one addressable cause' turns a vague error pile into rankable action items, the best ROI.
Stratifying usually shows the opposite — the bulk is often a targeted, fixable cause, no rebuild needed.
Splitting numbers isn't cosmetics; it's for localization and prioritization — switch tools only when there's no dominant cause.

termDefinitions.term: feature coverage gap / 特征覆盖缺口
termDefinitions.meaning: 某类样本缺少判别所需的特征信号，是一种可定向修复的失败根因。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature coverage gap is when a class lacks the feature signal needed to discriminate it, a targeted-fixable root cause.

scenario: 某个错误类别的 FN 很多，你想判断到底是「数据不够」还是「特征/架构不行」。你画了这一类的 learning curve（误差 vs 训练数据量）。
scenario_en: One error category has many FNs; to decide 'not enough data' vs 'feature/architecture gap', you plot its learning curve (error vs training-data volume).
q: learning curve 平掉（加数据不再降 FN）说明根因是什么？
q_en: If the learning curve flattens (more data no longer cuts FNs), what's the root cause?
why: 加数据不再降错误说明瓶颈不在数据量，而在特征或架构——模型手里根本没有能分开这类的信号。此时该补特征/换架构，堆样本是白花钱。
why_en: If more data stops reducing FNs, the bottleneck is features or architecture, not data volume, so add features or change the model rather than pile on samples.
tradeoff: 曲线仍在降→加数据有用 vs 曲线已平→补特征/换架构（加数据无效）
whenOtherWins: 如果 learning curve 还在明显下降，说明就是数据量不足，这时多标该类样本才是对的修复。
options: 说明还得再多加数据，只是加的量不够，继续堆样本迟早会降
说明瓶颈在特征或架构（缺可判别信号），该补特征/换架构，堆样本无效
说明标签全错，唯一出路是重标整个数据集
说明模型过拟合，加正则就能让这类 FN 下降
options_en: It means you still need more data — just not enough was added; keep piling on samples and it'll drop eventually.
It means the bottleneck is features or architecture (no discriminative signal), so add features or change the model; more samples won't help.
It means all the labels are wrong, and the only path is relabeling the entire dataset.
It means the model is overfitting, and adding regularization will drop these FNs.
optionExplanations: 曲线已平就是「加数据边际收益→0」的信号，再堆样本还是平，不是量不够的问题。
对；曲线平掉说明信息瓶颈在特征/架构，不是数据量；此时补信号才对症。
标签噪声是另一类根因，需要看一致性/重标抽样验证，learning curve 平不能直接推出「全错」。
过拟合表现为训练误差低、验证误差高的间隙，不是 learning curve 随数据量平掉的形状。
optionExplanations_en: A flat curve is the signal that marginal data value is ~0; more samples stay flat — it's not a 'not enough' problem.
Correct — a flat curve means the info bottleneck is features/architecture, not volume; adding signal is the right fix.
Label noise is a different root cause needing agreement/relabel checks; a flat curve alone can't conclude 'all wrong'.
Overfitting shows as a train-vs-validation error gap, not a learning curve flattening with more data.

termDefinitions.term: learning-curve analysis / 学习曲线分析
termDefinitions.meaning: 看某类误差随训练数据量的变化，判断加数据还有没有边际收益。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Learning-curve analysis inspects how a category's error changes with training-data volume to judge if more data still has marginal value.

scenario: 做搜索/推荐排序模型的错误分析，输出是一个有序列表而不是单个类别标签。
scenario_en: Doing error analysis for a search/recommendation ranking model whose output is an ordered list, not a single class label.
q: 为什么排序模型不能只靠混淆矩阵，要改看 hard negatives / hard positives？
q_en: Why does ranking need hard negatives/positives instead of just a confusion matrix?
why: 排序输出是有序列表，没有干脆的正/负判定，混淆矩阵不适用。改看模型「最自信却错」的样例：hard negative（无关项排很高）、hard positive（高相关项排很低），从这些极端错例里读出可修复的模式。
why_en: Ranking outputs an ordered list with no crisp positive/negative call, so inspect the most confidently wrong items — hard negatives ranked high and hard positives ranked low.
options: 混淆矩阵在排序里更准，只是计算慢，所以改用 hard example 抽样
排序输出是有序列表、没有干脆的正/负判定，改看『最自信却错』的 hard neg/hard pos 才能读出模式
排序模型没有错误可分析，只能看线上 CTR
hard example 只是混淆矩阵的另一种叫法，本质相同
options_en: The confusion matrix is more accurate for ranking, just slow, so you switch to hard-example sampling.
Ranking outputs an ordered list with no crisp positive/negative call, so inspect the most-confidently-wrong hard negatives/positives to read patterns.
Ranking models have no analyzable errors — you can only look at live CTR.
Hard examples are just another name for the confusion matrix; they're the same thing.
optionExplanations: 不是快慢问题——排序没有二分类判定，混淆矩阵的 TP/FP/FN/TN 框架本身就套不上。
对；有序列表要看极端错例的位置（无关项冲顶、相关项沉底），从中读出 popularity/position/cold-start 等模式。
排序当然可做错误分析，hard neg/pos 分析就是它的专属工具，不是只能看 CTR。
hard example 分析看的是排序位置上的错误，和混淆矩阵的分类计数是两码事。
optionExplanations_en: It's not about speed — ranking has no binary call, so the TP/FP/FN/TN frame simply doesn't apply.
Correct — for an ordered list you inspect extreme errors by position (irrelevant on top, relevant sunk), revealing popularity/position/cold-start patterns.
Ranking absolutely supports error analysis; hard neg/pos analysis is its dedicated tool, not just CTR-watching.
Hard-example analysis inspects positional errors in a ranking, a different thing from the confusion matrix's classification counts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本该排低的无关项却被模型打高分排进前列（如榜首的标题党）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hard negative is an irrelevant item the model wrongly scores high and ranks near the top (e.g. clickbait in top results).

termDefinitions.meaning: 本该排高的高相关项却被打低分沉到后面（如第三页的完美小众商品）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hard positive is a highly-relevant item the model wrongly scores low and buries deep (e.g. a perfect niche product on page 3).

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率：曝光中被点击的比例，常被排序模型当训练信号，但含偏差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR (Click-Through Rate) is clicks over impressions, often used as a ranking signal but carrying bias.

scenario: 复盘排序模型时，要区分两种最自信的错误：无关项冲到前列，和高相关项被压到后面。
scenario_en: Reviewing a ranking model, distinguish two confident errors: irrelevant items surging to the top vs highly-relevant items pushed to the back.
q: hard negative 和 hard positive 分别指什么？
q_en: What are hard negatives versus hard positives?
why: hard negative = 无关项被打高分排进前列（标题党冲上 top-5，用户秒退）；hard positive = 高相关项被打低分沉底（完美小众商品在第三页）。前者暴露「不该高的高了」，后者暴露「该高的没上来」。
why_en: A hard negative is an irrelevant item ranked too high, while a hard positive is a highly-relevant item ranked too low.
tradeoff: hard negative（无关项冲顶，precision 端问题）vs hard positive（相关项沉底，recall/覆盖端问题）
options: hard negative = 高相关项排太低；hard positive = 无关项排太高
hard negative = 无关项被打高分排进前列；hard positive = 高相关项被打低分沉到后面
两者都指训练中难分的样本，和排序位置无关
hard negative 指负样本太多，hard positive 指正样本太多，是类别不平衡问题
options_en: Hard negative = highly-relevant item ranked too low; hard positive = irrelevant item ranked too high.
Hard negative = irrelevant item scored high and ranked near the top; hard positive = highly-relevant item scored low and buried.
Both mean hard-to-separate training samples, unrelated to ranking position.
Hard negative means too many negatives, hard positive too many positives — a class-imbalance issue.
optionExplanations: 定义弄反了：negative 是「本该负却被高排」，positive 是「本该正却被低排」。
对；用一句记：negative 冲顶（不该高的高了），positive 沉底（该高的没上来）。
它们恰恰是按排序位置定义的极端错例，不是抽象的『难分样本』。
这是类别不平衡的概念，和 hard neg/pos 分析的『按位置看错例』无关。
optionExplanations_en: The definitions are swapped: negative is 'should be low but ranked high', positive is 'should be high but ranked low'.
Correct — mnemonic: negatives surge to the top (shouldn't be high), positives sink to the bottom (should be high but aren't).
They are precisely extreme errors defined by ranking position, not abstract 'hard-to-separate' samples.
That's class imbalance, unrelated to hard neg/pos analysis of positional errors.

scenario: 推荐排序里，一批热门但和当前用户无关的内容总被打高分冲进 top-5，用户点进去秒退（hard negative）。
scenario_en: In recommendation ranking, popular-but-irrelevant items keep surging into top-5 and users bounce instantly (hard negatives).
q: 这种「过度依赖全局热度」的 hard negative 该怎么修？
q_en: How to fix this 'over-indexing on global popularity' hard negative?
why: 根因是 popularity bias：模型过度依赖全局 CTR。修法在后处理加校准层 / 多样性重排器，把热度信号压回合理权重，而不是让全局热门无脑冲顶。
why_en: The root cause is popularity bias over-indexing on global CTR, fixed by a calibration layer or diversity re-ranker in post-processing.
tradeoff: 加校准/多样性重排（压热度、提相关）vs 不处理（全局热门霸榜、个性化失效）
whenOtherWins: 如果业务本身就要主推热门（如首页热榜、促销位），那么高热度排前是符合目标的，不该压。
options: 把模型容量加大，让它自己学会不迷信热度
在后处理加校准层 / 多样性重排器，把过高的全局热度权重压回合理范围
直接删掉所有热门内容，只推冷门以示公平
调低学习率重训，热度偏差就会消失
options_en: Enlarge the model so it learns on its own not to over-trust popularity.
Add a calibration layer / diversity re-ranker in post-processing to pull the over-weighted global popularity back to a reasonable range.
Just delete all popular content and recommend only obscure items for fairness.
Lower the learning rate and retrain, and the popularity bias will vanish.
optionExplanations: 加容量不改变训练信号里的热度偏差，模型往往学得更死地拟合全局 CTR。
对；popularity bias 是后处理层能直接治的——校准/多样性重排在打分后把热度拉回，定向且低成本。
一刀切删热门会误伤真正相关的热门项，把偏差矫枉过正成另一种失真。
调学习率是优化细节，不触及「特征/信号过度依赖全局热度」这个根因。
optionExplanations_en: More capacity doesn't change the popularity bias in the training signal; the model often fits global CTR even harder.
Correct — popularity bias is directly treatable in post-processing: a calibration/diversity re-ranker pulls popularity back after scoring, targeted and cheap.
Deleting all popular items hurts genuinely relevant popular ones, over-correcting into another distortion.
Tuning the learning rate is an optimization detail that doesn't touch the root cause of over-relying on global popularity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 排序过度依赖全局热度/CTR，导致热门内容不分场景地被排前。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Popularity bias is ranking over-relying on global popularity/CTR, pushing popular items to the top regardless of context.

termDefinitions.term: diversity re-ranker / 多样性重排器
termDefinitions.meaning: 在打分后重排结果、提升多样性、压制单一信号（如热度）霸榜的后处理层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A diversity re-ranker is a post-processing layer that reorders results to boost diversity and stop one signal (e.g. popularity) from dominating.

scenario: 排序模型的特征里编码了「内容当时展示的位置」，结果高位内容天然获得更多点击、又反过来喂进训练，形成反馈环（hard negative）。
scenario_en: The ranking features encode 'display position at the time'; high slots get more clicks, which feed back into training — a feedback loop (hard negative).
q: 这种 position bias leakage 该怎么治？
q_en: How to fix this position-bias leakage?
why: 位置作为特征泄漏进模型，会把「排在前所以被点」误学成「相关所以被点」，形成自我强化环。修法是训练时做位置去偏——用逆倾向加权（IPW）把位置带来的点击优势除掉。
why_en: Position leaks in as a feature and gets mislearned as relevance, so debias at training time with inverse propensity weighting to remove the position advantage.
tradeoff: 训练时位置去偏 IPW（除掉位置红利，学真相关）vs 保留位置特征（简单但反馈环放大偏差）
whenOtherWins: 如果你显式想建模「位置对点击的影响」本身（如做位置价值评估），则位置特征该保留，只是不能污染相关性打分。
options: 把展示位置作为更强的特征喂进去，让模型更好地利用位置信息
训练时做位置去偏，用逆倾向加权（IPW）除掉高位带来的点击优势
只在后处理随机打乱结果顺序，用随机性抵消位置偏差
忽略它，位置偏差会随数据量增大自动被平均掉
options_en: Feed display position as an even stronger feature so the model uses position info better.
Debias position at training time using inverse propensity weighting (IPW) to remove the click advantage of high slots.
Just randomly shuffle results in post-processing to cancel position bias with randomness.
Ignore it — position bias averages out on its own as data grows.
optionExplanations: 把位置喂得更强只会加剧泄漏，模型更依赖『排在前』这个和真相关无关的信号。
对；IPW 按位置的点击倾向反向加权，把高位红利除掉，让模型学到真正的相关性。
线上随机打乱伤害用户体验且不改训练信号，反馈环照样在数据里累积。
反馈环是自我强化的，数据越多偏差越被放大，不会自动平掉。
optionExplanations_en: Feeding position harder worsens the leakage; the model leans more on 'ranked high', a signal unrelated to true relevance.
Correct — IPW inversely weights by position click-propensity, removing the high-slot bonus so the model learns true relevance.
Random shuffling online hurts UX and doesn't change the training signal; the loop still accumulates in the data.
The feedback loop is self-reinforcing — more data amplifies the bias, it does not average out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容因展示位置靠前而多被点，模型误把位置当相关性信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Position bias is items getting more clicks because they're shown higher, with the model mistaking position for relevance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 逆倾向加权：按样本被观测/点击的倾向的倒数加权，抵消位置等展示偏差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IPW (Inverse Propensity Weighting) weights samples by the inverse of their observation/click propensity to cancel display biases like position.

scenario: 推荐里，历史交互稀疏的新商品总被打低分沉到后面，即使内容上和用户很匹配（hard positive）。
scenario_en: In recommendation, new items with sparse interaction history get scored low and buried, even when content-wise they match the user (hard positive).
q: 这种 cold-start 的 hard positive 该怎么修？
q_en: How to fix this cold-start hard positive?
why: 冷启动根因是缺协同/历史信号，模型没东西可依赖。修法是加强内容特征，或用双塔结构 + 一个鲁棒的 item tower，让新商品靠内容表征也能被正确排上来，而不是等它攒够交互。
why_en: Cold-start hard positives lack collaborative history, so strengthen content features or use a two-tower model with a robust item tower to rank them on content alone.
tradeoff: 强内容特征 / 双塔鲁棒 item tower（新品靠内容就能上榜）vs 只用交互信号（新品永远冷启动沉底）
whenOtherWins: 如果商品交互历史其实很快就积累（高流量平台、秒级反馈），短暂冷启动可容忍，靠交互信号即可，不必重构塔。
options: 调低分类阈值，让所有低分商品都往上提一点
加强内容特征，或用双塔 + 鲁棒 item tower，让新商品靠内容表征也能被正确排上来
把新商品直接固定加权到前排，绕过模型打分
等它自然积累足够交互再说，冷启动无法在建模层解决
options_en: Lower the classification threshold so every low-scored item gets bumped up a bit.
Strengthen content features, or use a two-tower model with a robust item tower so new items rank on content representation alone.
Hard-code a fixed boost putting new items at the top, bypassing the model score.
Just wait for them to accumulate enough interactions — cold-start can't be solved at the modeling layer.
optionExplanations: 全局降阈值会无差别抬升所有低分项，噪声和真相关一起上来，不解决『新品缺信号』。
对；缺协同信号就补内容信号——鲁棒 item tower 让新品用内容 embedding 参与排序，定向治冷启动。
固定加权硬顶前排会牺牲相关性、伤害体验，是绕过问题不是解决问题。
冷启动完全可在建模层缓解（内容特征/双塔），干等会持续损失新品曝光。
optionExplanations_en: A global threshold drop lifts every low-scored item indiscriminately, pulling noise up with signal and not fixing 'new items lack signal'.
Correct — missing collaborative signal is met with content signal: a robust item tower lets new items rank via content embeddings, targeting cold-start.
A fixed top boost sacrifices relevance and hurts UX — bypassing the problem, not solving it.
Cold-start can be mitigated at the modeling layer (content features/two-tower); just waiting keeps losing new-item exposure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新用户或新商品缺乏历史交互信号，模型难以给出准确预测。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cold-start is when a new user or item lacks historical interaction signal, making accurate prediction hard.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户塔和物品塔各自编码成 embedding，取内积做匹配的检索/排序结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-tower model encodes user and item into separate embeddings and matches them by inner product for retrieval/ranking.

scenario: 搜索排序里，罕见/长尾查询的表征很弱，相关结果被压低（hard positive），常见查询却很好。
scenario_en: In search ranking, rare/long-tail queries have weak representations and their relevant results get suppressed (hard positive), while common queries are fine.
q: 长尾查询导致的 hard positive 该怎么修？
q_en: How to fix hard positives from long-tail queries?
why: 长尾查询训练样本稀、表征弱。修法是查询扩展（同义词/改写补足信号）或用 embedding 做语义匹配，让罕见查询也能匹配到语义相近的相关文档，而不是死磕字面。
why_en: Long-tail queries are data-sparse with weak representations, so use query expansion or embedding-based semantic matching to reach relevant docs beyond literal terms.
tradeoff: 查询扩展 / 语义 embedding 匹配（补足长尾信号）vs 纯字面匹配（罕见查询表征弱、漏相关）
whenOtherWins: 如果查询本身高频、字面匹配已足够精准，强行做语义扩展反而引入噪声、降 precision，此时保持字面匹配更好。
options: 只给高频查询优化，长尾查询流量小可以忽略
做查询扩展（同义词/改写）或用 embedding 语义匹配，让罕见查询也能匹配语义相近的相关文档
把长尾查询一律返回全局热门结果，反正它们没有明确意图
对长尾查询直接报错让用户改写，避免给出弱结果
options_en: Only optimize high-frequency queries; long-tail traffic is small and can be ignored.
Use query expansion (synonyms/rewrites) or embedding-based semantic matching so rare queries reach semantically similar relevant docs.
Return global-popular results for all long-tail queries since they have no clear intent anyway.
Throw an error on long-tail queries asking users to rephrase, avoiding weak results.
optionExplanations: 长尾累加起来往往是很大一块流量，忽略它等于放弃相当比例的相关性提升。
对；长尾弱表征就补语义信号——扩展/embedding 让罕见查询跨越字面匹配到相关文档，定向治长尾。
无脑返回全局热门抛弃了查询意图，把 hard positive 问题换成了不相关问题。
报错逼用户改写是把系统缺陷转嫁给用户，体验差且不解决表征弱的根因。
optionExplanations_en: Long-tail queries sum to a large traffic share; ignoring them forfeits a sizable relevance gain.
Correct — weak long-tail representation is met with semantic signal: expansion/embeddings let rare queries reach relevant docs beyond literal terms.
Blindly returning global-popular discards query intent, swapping the hard-positive problem for an irrelevance problem.
Erroring to force a rephrase offloads the system flaw onto users, poor UX and no fix for weak representation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 出现频率很低、样本稀疏的查询，模型对它的表征通常较弱。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A long-tail query occurs rarely with sparse data, so the model's representation of it is usually weak.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用同义词、改写、相关词补充原查询，增强对稀疏查询的信号覆盖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Query expansion augments the original query with synonyms/rewrites/related terms to boost signal coverage for sparse queries.

scenario: 面试里给排序系统做设计，你想把 hard negative 和 hard positive 分析都用上。
scenario_en: Designing a ranking system in an interview, you want to use both hard-negative and hard-positive analysis.
q: 面试里该把 hard-negative 和 hard-positive 分别定位成什么角色？
q_en: In an interview, what role should you frame hard negatives vs hard positives as?
why: hard-negative mining 是训练策略——把最难的负例喂进训练让模型学会区分；hard-positive 分析是评估策略——用被压低的相关项检查模型漏了什么。一个改训练、一个改评估，别混用。
why_en: Frame hard-negative mining as a training strategy and hard-positive analysis as an evaluation strategy — one shapes training, the other shapes evaluation.
tradeoff: hard-negative mining（训练侧：喂难负例提升判别）vs hard-positive 分析（评估侧：查漏检的相关项）
options: 两者都当训练策略，一起塞进 loss 里训
hard-negative mining = 训练策略（喂难负例提判别）；hard-positive 分析 = 评估策略（查被压低的相关项）
两者都只是评估指标，不影响训练
hard-negative 用于评估、hard-positive 用于训练，正好互换
options_en: Treat both as training strategies and stuff them into the loss together.
Hard-negative mining = training strategy (feed hard negatives to sharpen discrimination); hard-positive analysis = evaluation strategy (find suppressed relevant items).
Both are just evaluation metrics with no effect on training.
Use hard negatives for evaluation and hard positives for training — the swap works out.
optionExplanations: 都当训练策略会丢掉 hard-positive 的评估价值——它是用来发现『模型漏了哪些相关项』的诊断镜。
对；分工清晰：难负例进训练提判别，漏检的正例进评估查覆盖，正是文中建议的组合拳。
hard-negative mining 明确是训练策略（改变训练分布），不只是评估指标。
角色说反了：mining 面向训练、hard-positive 分析面向评估，互换就错位了。
optionExplanations_en: Making both training strategies loses hard positives' evaluation value — the diagnostic lens for 'which relevant items did the model miss'.
Correct — clean division: hard negatives sharpen training discrimination, missed positives audit coverage in evaluation, the recommended combo.
Hard-negative mining is explicitly a training strategy (it reshapes the training distribution), not merely an evaluation metric.
The roles are reversed: mining is for training and hard-positive analysis is for evaluation; swapping misplaces both.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主动挑出最难区分的负例加入训练，逼模型学会更细的判别边界。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hard-negative mining actively selects the hardest-to-distinguish negatives for training to force a sharper decision boundary.

q: 把面试里讲错误分析的 4 步模板排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the 4-step template for presenting error analysis in an interview:
steps: 假设最大类别的根因，点名具体组件（缺特征→特征管线缺该实体的结构化数据）
先报 aggregate 指标 + 它的局限（precision 92%，但掩盖了某些 segment 的失败）
提出针对性修复 + 验证计划（连到只覆盖受影响 segment 的 A/B 测试）
给出错误分类和占比（45% 缺特征、30% 标签噪声、25% 分布漂移）
why: 顺序：先说均值+局限 → 再给分类占比 → 假设最大类根因点名组件 → 提针对性修复+验证。这条链把「我看到问题」升级成「我知道根因并能验证修复」，是 staff 级表达。
why_en: State the aggregate and its limit, give categorized proportions, hypothesize the largest category's root cause by naming a component, then propose a targeted fix with a validation plan.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户分成对照组和实验组比较指标差异，用来验证一个改动是否真的有效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An A/B test splits users into control and treatment to compare metrics and verify whether a change truly helps.

scenario: 面试里你已经说完「45% 失败来自缺特征，根因在特征管线」，接下来要收尾这段错误分析。
scenario_en: In the interview you've said '45% of failures are missing-feature, root cause in the feature pipeline'; now you close the error-analysis segment.
q: 第 4 步收尾该给什么，才显出 staff 级完整度？
q_en: What should the closing 4th step give to show staff-level completeness?
why: 收尾要给「针对性修复 + 验证计划」：把修复连到一个只覆盖受影响 segment 的 A/B 测试，证明你不仅会诊断，还能闭环验证。只提修复不提验证，链条是断的。
why_en: Close with a targeted fix plus a validation plan — an A/B test scoped to the affected segment — proving you close the loop, not just diagnose.
tradeoff: 修复 + 定向 A/B 验证（闭环、可证伪）vs 只提修复（听起来像猜、无法验证）
whenOtherWins: 如果受影响 segment 太小、A/B 拿不到统计功效，可先用离线回放/影子评估验证，再决定是否上线小流量实验。
options: 宣布问题已解决，直接进入下一个话题
提出针对性修复，并连到一个只覆盖受影响 segment 的 A/B 测试来验证
把整个模型推倒重训，证明你敢下重手
列一堆可能的修复方向，但不说怎么验证哪个有效
options_en: Declare the problem solved and move to the next topic.
Propose a targeted fix and tie it to an A/B test scoped to just the affected segment to validate it.
Retrain the whole model from scratch to show you dare to go big.
List many possible fix directions but never say how to validate which one works.
optionExplanations: 没验证就宣布解决，面试官会觉得你只会诊断不会闭环，恰恰漏掉 staff 级的那半。
对；把修复钉到一个 scoped A/B 上，既定向又可证伪，展示完整的诊断-修复-验证闭环。
推倒重训是最贵的动作，且和『缺特征在特征管线』这个定向根因不匹配，杀鸡用牛刀。
只列方向不谈验证，等于回到『猜』；错误分析的价值就在于把猜变成可验证的行动。
optionExplanations_en: Declaring victory without validation reads as diagnose-only, missing exactly the staff-level half.
Correct — pinning the fix to a scoped A/B is targeted and falsifiable, showing the full diagnose-fix-validate loop.
A full retrain is the most expensive move and mismatched to a targeted 'missing-feature in the pipeline' cause — overkill.
Listing directions without validation is back to guessing; error analysis's value is turning guesses into verifiable actions.

scenario: 45 分钟的 ML 系统设计面试里，错误分析只是其中一环，你不能讲太久。
scenario_en: In a 45-minute ML system design interview, error analysis is just one part — you can't dwell on it.
q: 错误分析这段大概该控制在多长，意味着怎么组织内容？
q_en: How long should error analysis take, and what does that imply for structure?
why: 大约 2–3 分钟——这是给定的时间预算不是公式推导。它意味着你必须用固定 4 步模板压缩表达，简洁本身就是深度的体现，练时用计时器逼自己收敛。
why_en: About 2–3 minutes — a given budget, not a computed number, meaning you compress into the fixed 4-step template where conciseness signals depth.
options: 全程 20 分钟，把每个错误类别都展开细讲，越详细越显专业
大约 2–3 分钟：用固定 4 步模板压缩表达，简洁即深度，练时用计时器逼收敛
一句话带过（10 秒），错误分析不重要，把时间全给架构
没有时间概念，讲到面试官打断为止
options_en: A full 20 minutes, expanding every error category in detail — the more detail the more professional.
About 2–3 minutes: compress into the fixed 4-step template where conciseness signals depth; practice with a timer.
One sentence (10 seconds) — error analysis isn't important, give all the time to architecture.
No sense of time — talk until the interviewer cuts you off.
optionExplanations: 20 分钟会吃掉整场面试，展开每一类反而暴露你不会抓重点，是负信号。
对；2–3 分钟是产品级时间预算，逼你用 4 步模板讲清均值→占比→根因→修复+验证。
10 秒带过又走到另一个极端——错误分析恰是 L5 成熟度信号，值得 2–3 分钟。
没有时间控制会挤掉后面的架构/扩展环节，面试是限时的资源分配。
optionExplanations_en: 20 minutes eats the whole interview, and expanding every category shows you can't prioritize — a negative signal.
Correct — 2–3 minutes is a product-level budget forcing the 4-step template: aggregate to proportions to root cause to fix-plus-validation.
A 10-second brush-off swings to the other extreme — error analysis is an L5 maturity signal worth 2–3 minutes.
No time control crowds out later architecture/scaling; the interview is a timed resource allocation.

scenario: 面试官没有主动问错误分析，你已经讲完模型架构，还有时间。
scenario_en: The interviewer didn't ask about error analysis; you've finished the architecture and still have time.
q: 主动补一段错误分析计划，会传递什么信号？
q_en: What signal does volunteering an error-analysis plan send?
why: 不用问就主动给出错误分析计划，传递的是 L5-vs-L4 的成熟度：你不只会把模型搭出来，还预设了它会怎么失败、如何系统性诊断和改。这是资深工程师的默认动作。
why_en: Volunteering an error-analysis plan unprompted signals L5-over-L4 maturity — you anticipate how the model fails and how to diagnose it systematically.
options: 显得啰嗦，会拉低评价，最好等被问再讲
传递 L5-vs-L4 的成熟度：你会预设失败模式并系统性诊断，是资深默认动作
只有做过研究的人才配讲，工程岗讲了会显得越界
没有任何信号价值，面试官只看模型指标高不高
options_en: It seems verbose and lowers your rating — better wait to be asked.
It signals L5-over-L4 maturity: you anticipate failure modes and diagnose systematically — a senior default.
Only researchers should raise it; for an engineering role it looks out of scope.
It carries no signal value — the interviewer only cares whether the model's metrics are high.
optionExplanations: 简洁地主动给计划不是啰嗦，是主动权；等被问反而少了一次展示成熟度的机会。
对；主动预设失败并给诊断计划，正是区分 L5 和 L4 的行为，面试官很吃这套。
错误分析是工程岗核心技能，不是研究专利，讲它恰好证明你懂系统落地。
面试评估的是工程判断而非只看指标，主动错误分析正是高价值判断信号。
optionExplanations_en: Concisely volunteering a plan isn't verbosity, it's initiative; waiting to be asked forfeits a chance to show maturity.
Correct — proactively anticipating failures with a diagnosis plan is exactly the L5-vs-L4 behavior interviewers reward.
Error analysis is a core engineering skill, not a research monopoly; raising it proves you understand real deployment.
Interviews assess engineering judgment, not just metrics; proactive error analysis is a high-value judgment signal.

scenario: Categorize 阶段要给失败打 MECE 标签，你在列可用的失败类别桶。
scenario_en: In Categorize you're listing the MECE failure buckets to label failures with.
q: 以下哪些是文中给出的、合理的失败类别桶？(多选)
q_en: Which of these are the reasonable failure buckets from the lesson? (multiple)
why: 文中的类别桶都是能追到具体组件的根因：缺特征→特征管线、标签噪声→数据标注、分布漂移→训练/线上分布、模型容量→架构、serving 延迟截断→推理路径。「GPU 太贵」是成本问题，不是失败诊断类别。
why_en: The buckets each trace to a component — missing-feature, label-noise, distribution-shift, model-capacity, serving-latency-truncation — while 'GPU too expensive' is a cost issue, not a failure category.
options: 缺特征（missing feature）——追到特征管线
标签噪声（label noise）——追到数据标注质量
serving 延迟截断——为满足延迟预算截断特征/计算，追到推理路径
GPU 太贵——追到采购预算
options_en: Missing feature — traces to the feature pipeline.
Label noise — traces to data-annotation quality.
Serving latency truncation — features/compute cut to meet a latency budget, traces to the inference path.
GPU is too expensive — traces to the procurement budget.
optionExplanations: 对；缺特征是最常见的可定向修复根因，直接指向特征管线该补什么信号。
对；标签噪声把错误标签当真值，污染训练，追到标注流程做一致性质控。
对；延迟截断为赶预算牺牲了特征/计算，是能追到推理路径的真实失败类别。
错；GPU 贵是成本/资源问题，不是某个预测为什么错的诊断类别，混进来会破坏 MECE。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — missing feature is the most common targeted-fixable root cause, pointing straight at what signal the feature pipeline lacks.
Correct — label noise treats wrong labels as truth, polluting training; trace it to annotation and add agreement QC.
Correct — latency truncation sacrifices features/compute to meet a budget, a real failure category traceable to the inference path.
Incorrect — GPU cost is a resource/budget issue, not a diagnostic category for why a prediction was wrong, and it breaks MECE.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练数据里的错误标签，被当成真值会系统性误导模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Label noise is incorrect labels in training data that, treated as truth, systematically mislead the model.
